ops.title: daemonkit v0.20.6 has no GitHub release object — wrong-key tag signature, immutable-tag ruleset blocks re-signing; accepted
ops.body:
The v0.20.6 baseline tag (85d53fd) was signed with the repo-default EDDSA key (4E7C358CCBEBA2D5, yasyf@poetic.com) instead of the fleet release key (RSA F3299DE3FE0F6C3CF2B66BFBF7ECDD88A700D73A, yasyfm@gmail.com), so Release run 30178198820 failed at verify-tag-on-main and no GitHub release was published for v0.20.6. Latest published daemonkit release remains v0.20.5.

A corrected re-signed tag was prepared, but the repo's "Immutable v* release tags" ruleset (id 19649430) rejects both tag update and deletion — correctly: that immutability protects fleet pin integrity, and it is why synckit (v0.36.0→v0.36.1) and cc-patch (v0.12.0→v0.12.1) re-cut new versions after the same wrong-key failure instead of mutating tags. Cutting v0.20.7 for this would violate the release freeze and force 11 downstream repins for a cosmetic artifact.

**Decision: accepted as-is.** Functional convergence is unaffected — proxy.golang.org serves v0.20.6 (immutable module cache, Ref refs/tags/v0.20.6), all 11 downstream go.mods pin and build it green, daemonkit has no brew/plugin/asset distribution, and the CHANGELOG entry for 0.20.6 is on main. The missing artifact is release notes only.

**For the next daemonkit release (post-freeze):** tag with explicit `-u F3299DE3FE0F6C3CF2B66BFBF7ECDD88A700D73A` and `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Yasyf Mohamedali' GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='yasyfm@gmail.com'` (the local clone's git config defaults to the wrong key). If the release object for v0.20.6 is ever wanted, the recipe (owner-only, deliberate): temporarily disable ruleset 19649430, `git push origin :refs/tags/v0.20.6`, re-create the tag signed with the trusted key on 85d53fd with message "daemonkit v0.20.6", push, re-enable the ruleset; the Release workflow re-runs on the tag push.
